note: Maps an ingredient category onto the derived base-spirit facet. This is the most-used browsing axis for cocktails and it is never hand-tagged on a drink: it is read off the ingredient list and ranked by how much alcohol each category contributes, so nobody can forget to apply it and it cannot go stale when an ingredient is swapped.
partialNote: The map is deliberately PARTIAL. A category is an ingredient property that also feeds My Bar grouping and filtering; a base spirit is what a drink is built out of. Categories that are only ever modifiers are left out, and leaving them out is the point: contributions are summed per category, so mapping two modifiers into one bucket lets them outvote the base. Equal parts gin, bitter aperitivo and sweet vermouth puts 12 ml of alcohol in from the gin and 12.3 ml in from the other two, and the drink would report as an aperitivo drink rather than the gin drink every reader looks for it as.

deliberatelyUnmapped.vermouth: A modifier, never a base. A drink built on vermouth alone is a wine drink, and its own category already carries it for filtering.
deliberatelyUnmapped.quinquina: Same as vermouth — an aromatised wine used to modify, not to build on.
